solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Departs pub game that's over, tucked into beer, ready for the off?

indicators.note: a game that is over has been turned over, so the word for it is read from the end back
something tucked into a thing sits inside it, so these letters go within the drink

blocks.note: darts is the classic game played in a pub
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker leaves the pub once the darts match ends, a beer inside them, keen to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departs' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is just the timetable letter. 'The off' is the start of a race, and a rider sits with a leg on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting astride a horse or bike, legs on either side, is poised to set off.

clue.text: Losing run, valour wasted, runner admits, 'One's skewered'

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped, so a letter comes out of the next word
wasted letters are ruined and reshaped into a new order
to admit is to let in, so the outer piece takes the other letters inside it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
a ski is a runner that slides over snow

explanation.surface: A runner who has lost a race and their courage is somehow impaled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like the athlete of the surface, but it is the thing a skier glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvlaki is a Greek dish of meat chunks cooked on a skewer, so it is something skewered.

clue.text: Add as free extra, sacrificing win all the way

indicators.note: sacrificing something is giving it up, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to throw in is to add something free
W is the abbreviation for win

explanation.surface: A sports promoter throws in a bonus but gives up a victory to go the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: THROW loses W to leave THRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thro is an informal short spelling of through, as in through and through, meaning completely.

clue.text: Race meeting producing great reverberating cheers

indicators.note: something reverberating is shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A race day where the crowd roars with loud, echoing cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event consisting of a series of boat races.

clue.text: Ambitious Verdi composed opening for Nabucco

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh
the opening of a word is its very start, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the opera's name

explanation.surface: The ambitious Verdi wrote the overture to his opera Nabucco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' sits naturally with a composer, but here it signals the rearrangement of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A driven person is strongly motivated to succeed, which is what ambitious means.

clue.text: Longing I'll have to be housed in nice home (but not special)

indicators.note: something housed in another is kept inside it, so the single letter goes within
but not means without, so one letter is left out

blocks.note: the I of the clue, which is to be lodged inside
des res is estate-agent jargon for a desirable residence
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to move into a lovely house, though not a particularly special one.
explanation.walkthrough: DES RES, British estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence, drops one S to give DESRE, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire and longing are both nouns for a strong wish for something.

clue.text: Part of the furniture in hall at Chequers?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: found across letters 4-8 of 'hall at Chequers'

explanation.surface: Spotting a piece of furniture in the hall at Chequers, the British prime minister's country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Door furniture means handles, knobs and fastenings; the surface wants tables and chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a door fastening, one of the fittings known collectively as door furniture.

clue.text: You may find elanet, first off, is mistaken for one

definitions.text: You may find elanet, first off, is mistaken for one

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed from the word before
mistaken suggests something got wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written; an elanet is a kite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher warns that one hawk is easily confused with another.
explanation.walkthrough: ELANET loses its E, and LANET with IS is rearranged. The whole clue also describes the bird: one bird of prey mistaken for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A staniel is a dialect name for the kestrel, a bird of prey that could be confused with a kite.

clue.text: Head of force, local or national

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of force
the local is British slang for your nearest pub

explanation.surface: A police chief must choose between local and national jurisdiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local or national' reads as a police choice; local is the pub and national is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native or citizen of Finland, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Alternation of generations? Teen miss is upset about one of them

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so those letters are scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
an age is a generation, one of the generations just mentioned

explanation.surface: A teenage girl is annoyed at the older generation in a family-tension scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' links the clue's halves, and 'them' points back to generations, so one of them is an AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Metagenesis is the biological term for the alternation of sexual and asexual phases in a life cycle.

clue.text: Synagogue elder, male brought in to teach formerly

indicators.note: brought in to means placed within, so the first piece sits inside the second

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
con is an obsolete verb meaning to teach or learn

explanation.surface: A senior figure at the synagogue, a man drafted in to give lessons in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cohen is a member of the Jewish priestly caste, given ritual honours in the synagogue.

clue.text: Scots tell tales about dodgy priest – it aids fundamental cleansing

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so these letters are taken apart and rearranged
about means around, so the outer word goes round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: clype is a Scots verb meaning to tell tales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scottish gossips spread stories about a shady cleric's purification ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fundamental' is a pun on the fundament, the buttocks: the cleansing is an enema.
explanation.definitionFit: A clyster-pipe is an old tube for giving an enema, which washes out the bowel.

clue.text: Tear manufactured with lie? Once the opposite thereof

indicators.note: manufactured means made up out of parts, so the letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a fake tear a kind of lie, or was it once the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thereof' points back to lie, so the definition is an old word for honesty, the opposite of a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtie is an archaic Spenserian word for sincerity or truthfulness, the reverse of falsehood.

clue.text: Nameless malady right inside ear – iodine applied

indicators.note: inside means within, so the single letter is put into the word for the body part

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
lug is a colloquial word for an ear
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: An unidentified illness inside the ear is treated with iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy, also spelt lurgi, is a joke illness from the British radio comedy The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: The lurgi is a humorous name for any vague, unspecified ailment, an illness without a real name.

clue.text: Attendant offloading minis to peddle

indicators.note: offloading means getting rid of a load, so these letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a ministrant is one who attends or serves, as at an altar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car-park attendant gets rid of the small cars in order to sell goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minis' looks like the little cars, but its letters are simply removed from the start of MINISTRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Trant is a dialect verb meaning to hawk goods about as a pedlar, so to peddle.

clue.text: Polymath of yore, one attending college in European capital

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letter for the institution goes within the city's name

blocks.note: a means one
C is the abbreviation for college
Vienna is the capital of Austria

explanation.surface: A medieval scholar studied at a college in a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One attending' says A stands next to what follows, C inside VIENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Avicenna, the Persian Ibn Sina, was an eleventh-century physician and philosopher of vast learning.

clue.text: Paint Pollock-style, singular, modern?

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
latter means more recent, hence modern

explanation.surface: Is painting in the drip manner of Jackson Pollock a unique and modern art?
explanation.walkthrough: Jackson Pollock was the American painter famous for dripping and splashing paint onto canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To slatter is to spill or splash carelessly, which describes Pollock's drip technique.

clue.text: Barley of a kind? Granary displays one but not garden

definitions.text: Granary displays one but not garden

blocks.note: first meaning: a variety of four-rowed barley

blocks.clueFragment: Granary displays one but not garden
blocks.note: second meaning: the word Granary, capitalised, begins with a ..., which the word garden does not

explanation.surface: A grain store shows off a type of barley that the garden lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the answer is BIG G: Granary is printed with a capital, garden with a small letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigg is a Scots and northern word for a hardy four-rowed barley, and also splits into the phrase for a capital letter.

clue.text: Old BBQ stuff, rank? One gets sick inside

indicators.note: one that gets something inside it takes it in, so these letters go within
inside confirms the sickness word goes within the rank word rather than beside it

blocks.note: a grade is a rank
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Rotten old barbecue food makes someone ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to the rank, which takes the sickness inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillade is an old word for grilled meat or a dish cooked on a grill, like barbecue fare.

clue.text: Mediterranean vessel departs in distinctive colours

blocks.note: a tartane is a single-masted Mediterranean sailing boat
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean ship sets sail flying its own colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartaned means dressed in tartan, the checked cloth whose pattern identifies a Scottish clan.

clue.text: Crewman grasping end of taffrail – it helped him climb aloft

indicators.note: grasping means holding within, so the sailor word wraps round the letter
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a rating is a sailor who is not an officer
last letter of taffrail

explanation.surface: A sailor clutches the end of the stern rail to haul himself up the rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Him' refers to the crewman, so the definition is the rope he climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratline (ratling) is one of the small ropes across a ship's shrouds forming a ladder up the rigging.

clue.text: Chap with a stick for measuring up early instrument

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a chap is a man
taken as written
a rod is a measuring stick and an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A man with a ruler sizes up an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandora is an old lute-like stringed instrument, an ancestor of the mandolin.

clue.text: Nail damaged after injury? Caper derivative required

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: harm is injury
taken as written

explanation.surface: After an injury, a damaged fingernail needs something from a caper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' suggests a lark or the pickled bud; here it is the bean-caper family of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmaline is an alkaloid obtained from harmel, wild rue of the bean-caper family.

clue.text: Once coated in oily stuff, a brand has head of match inserted

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that is used
a word that has something inserted holds it inside, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
to brand is to sear with a hot iron
first letter of match

explanation.surface: A branding iron caked in grease has a match stuck into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmear is an old-fashioned adjective meaning smeared over, as with grease or oil.

clue.text: Geometrical figures transforming hob rim

indicators.note: transforming means changing shape, so these letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Geometric patterns change the look of a cooker's rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi is the plural of rhombus, a four-sided shape with equal sides.

clue.text: What, we hear, does it dread getting from disgruntled guests?

definitions.text: What, we hear, does it dread getting from disgruntled guests?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: what such guests send is writs, legal summonses

explanation.surface: A posh hotel fears what unhappy guests might do.
explanation.walkthrough: Unhappy guests serve writs, and that word said aloud names the London luxury hotel that fears them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London, the sort that would worry about lawsuits from guests.

clue.text: Market forming circle in Indian city –see a white man there?

indicators.note: in means inside, so the round letter goes within the city name

blocks.note: O is circle-shaped
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
surface padding, with a bonus: gora is Hindi for a white man

explanation.surface: A bazaar in an Indian city where a white visitor stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail is a bonus: the answer also splits as A GORA, gora being Hindi for a white man.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the open marketplace and assembly area of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Bank, stony? One requiring injection of cash ultimately

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the letter goes within the word
ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: single means one
last letter of cash

explanation.surface: A bank that is broke needs a cash injection to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'cash' build a financial picture; stony suggests stony broke, but the bank is a pebbly beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, as on a stony beach or bank.

clue.text: Boil maybe GP treated with hot lemon

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a boil with a hot lemon drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmon is an inflammation of tissue with pus, of which a boil is one example.

clue.text: Where trawler is heading back when it's replaced line

indicators.note: replaced means one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a half-back, or half, is a player in a back position
L is the abbreviation for line
a is a dialect pronoun for he, she, it or they

explanation.surface: A trawler heads back after switching to a new line.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF loses its L and gains A. 'Back' is not a direction but a sports position.
explanation.definitionFit: A haaf is a deep-sea fishing ground off Shetland and Orkney, where a trawler would go.

clue.text: Stanza missing second half, Milton's botch

indicators.note: missing its second half means the latter half of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a quatrain is a four-line stanza

explanation.surface: Milton botched a verse that lacks its second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milton's' marks the word as one used by the poet John Milton.
explanation.definitionFit: Quat is an obsolete word for a pimple or boil, which Milton used; botch is an old term for a boil.

clue.text: Martial art I practise, ideal inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so the word for perfect goes into the phrase

blocks.note: I plus do, to practise
A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: A student says they practise a martial art and find it ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iaido is the Japanese martial art of drawing the sword swiftly from its scabbard.

clue.text: French university degree, one in French certainly

indicators.note: in means inside, so the single letter goes within the French word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for degree
a means one
oui is French for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone confirms getting a degree at a French university.
explanation.definitionFit: Douai is a town in northern France, historically home to a university and an English Catholic college.

clue.text: Uniting much of the ME, a prince back in lead

indicators.note: back means backwards, so these letters are read in reverse
in means inside, so the reversed letters go within the symbol

blocks.note: a plus rana, a Hindu prince
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Uniting most of the Middle East needs a prince to take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ME' is the Middle East; 'lead' looks like leadership but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan-Arab describes a movement to bring together all the Arab nations, much of the Middle East.

clue.text: Dictionary university's not allowed in? They'll have passed finals

indicators.note: not allowed in means barred, so that letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: a gradus is a Latin prosody dictionary, after Gradus ad Parnassum
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A dictionary barred from a university, read by students who passed their exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Grads is short for graduates, people who have passed their final examinations.

clue.text: Like many a vessel from Central America in trade at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trading ship from Central America is out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' reads as a ship, and many ships are keeled, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Carinated means keeled or having a ridge like a keel, as many boats have.
